premises.text: Consumer product companies waste significant marketing budgets on ineffective targeting.
premises.evidence_span: In the U.S. alone, consumer product companies spend $50 billion a year trying to convince you to buy more of their products. And they'll flat out tell you they know 50% of that budget is misspent and wasted on the wrong customers.

premises.text: Current marketing methods lack effective targeting for consumer product companies.
premises.evidence_span: The trouble is, they don't know which 50%.

premises.text: SnapDragon provides a product check-in game that engages users and rewards loyalty.
premises.evidence_span: SnapDragon is a product check-in game with a twist.

premises.text: The app unlocks a comic book adventure based on product check-ins.
premises.evidence_span: SnapDragon is a story that's unlocked by the things that you do.

premises.text: Users can share product check-ins on social media for real-time feedback.
premises.evidence_span: When you zap it, you can see exactly what your friends think about it.

premises.text: The app includes product leaderboards to enhance user engagement.
premises.evidence_span: we have product leaderboards, which we call fanships.

value.text: Consumer product marketing becomes more effective and engaging through targeted rewards and gamification.
value.evidence_span: By finally giving consumer product marketers the targeting tools that they need and wrapping the whole thing in this fun gaming experience, we want to fundamentally reinvent how consumer product companies market to their customers.

notes: No separate premises for the comic book content as it is part of the product check-in experience.
